text:
**Answer**

Based on the Office for National Statistics (ONS) *Domestic gas consumption* indicator (median consumption per meter, kWh), the unitary authority that experienced the greatest fall in domestic gas use between 2012 and 2023 is **Flintshire**.

| Local authority | 2012 kWh / meter (median) | 2023 kWh / meter (median) | Change (kWh) |
|-----------------|----------------------------|----------------------------|--------------|
| Flintshire | 12 096 kWh | 9 432 kWh | **–2 664 kWh** |
| County Durham | 10 627 kWh | 9 134 kWh | –1 493 kWh |
| Bedford | 9 442 kWh | 8 589 kWh | –853 kWh |
| North Lincolnshire | 9 813 kWh | 8 998 kWh | –815 kWh |
| Telford & Wrekin | 9 309 kWh | 9 030 kWh | –279 kWh |

*These figures are taken from the ONS “Domestic gas consumption” dataset (indicator *domestic-gas-consumption*). The values are median consumption per meter for the period 1 April 2012 – 31 March 2013 (reported as 2012–13) and for 1 April 2022 – 31 March 2023 (reported as 2022–23).*

The difference of **–2 664 kWh** is the largest drop among the five authorities listed, making Flintshire the unitary authority with the biggest decline in domestic gas consumption over the 2012‑2023 period.
